title: The journey
intent: Origin owner 2026-09-08: frame the platform as a customer journey of five, seven or nine single-letter steps, left to right, covering the whole end to end. Each step exposes the domains, entities and standards it needs, so anyone can say where they are. Customers walk it, and so do agents. Taken further here (proposed): every column is computed from the registry, the skills, the ontology, the examples and the litmus scorecard, so the journey doubles as the gap map.

actors.person: the customer: an engineer, operator or reviewer who hands work in and lives with the result
actors.agent: a unit of agent work, or an external agent at the fourth door, walking the same steps from the inside

steps.name: Ask
steps.person: I have intent. How do I hand it over from where I am, and what do I get back at once?
steps.agent: Which door am I entering by, who am I acting for, and what is my envelope?
steps.summary: Intent from any of the four doors becomes one validated envelope with an actor, a key and a correlation id, and the caller gets an acknowledgement at once.
steps.examples_why: area 1 Invocation / Entry Points -- 'How work enters the platform'; the step turns intent from any door into one validated envelope

steps.name: Bound
steps.person: What will this cost, what is it allowed to touch, and when does it run?
steps.agent: What is my ceiling, which rule decided I may act, and what schedule fired me?
steps.summary: The document is priced, its ceilings set, its policy decided and its schedule computed before anything is spent or any cell exists.
steps.examples_why: area 2 Orchestration & Control Plane -- 'Turn requests into work, apply policy, and coordinate agents'; the step prices, bounds, decides policy and computes schedule

steps.name: Contain
steps.person: Where does it run, what can it reach, and who says so?
steps.agent: What is my cell, what is mounted, which tools are bound, and what identity do I carry?
steps.summary: A cell is provisioned to the declared security profile, the contract and workspace are mounted, tools are bound and the unit carries an attested identity.
steps.examples_why: area 4 Execution & Runtime -- 'Run agents in isolated, repeatable, production-safe environments' -- with area 3 for the workspace and tool interface the step mounts and binds

steps.name: Do
steps.person: What happens in the sandbox on my behalf, and what if fifty run at once?
steps.agent: One turn: what did I get, which model class answered, which tool ran, and why did I stop?
steps.summary: The harness runs one turn inside the cell under the ceiling: a model class answers, tools are called, and the turn ends with a typed stop reason or a typed failure.
steps.examples_why: area 3 Core Agent -- 'One worker, one job'; the step runs one turn through the harness, a model class and the tools

steps.name: Evidence
steps.person: How do I see it from where I am, and how do I intervene?
steps.agent: What am I emitting, who is watching, and what happens when I must ask a person?
steps.summary: Everything the unit does leaves a correlated trail a person can watch from their own surface and steer by approving, editing, rejecting or answering.
steps.examples_why: area 6 Observe; the step is the correlated trail a person watches and steers by

steps.name: Finish
steps.person: How do I know it is finished, how does it reach production, and what happens next?
steps.agent: What did I produce, who judged it, what was attested, and what is my disposition?
steps.summary: The work product is judged against visible and hidden checks, attested, recorded in the tamper-evident log, and given a disposition that moves it toward production.
steps.examples_why: area 5 Assurance & Completion -- 'Validate results, admit outputs, and hand back to the caller'

steps.name: Grow
steps.person: What did the platform learn, and what changed because of it?
steps.agent: Which skill or template shaped me, was it measured, and which revision replaced it?
steps.summary: Usage, issues and outcomes feed the improvement loop, which revises templates and skills toward the target and proves each revision against the evaluation gate.
steps.examples_why: area 7 Self-Improvement; the step feeds usage and outcomes into the loop

examples_note: Steps name the nine areas under examples/reference/, not the seven journey areas archived on 2026-09-09. Each step's `examples_why` records what grounds the pairing: the step's own 'what happens here' text against the reference model's area title and subtitle. base-shared-services and rail-cross-cutting appear in no step on purpose -- examples/reference/README.md: base is 'used by every layer' and rail 'spans every layer', so they cut across the journey rather than sitting at a point in it.
